topic: Assignment and Compound Assignment Operators in Modern C++
explanation: In C++, assignment operators (=, +=, -=, *=, /=, %=, &=, |=, ^=, <<=, >>=) are used to modify objects by assigning new values. These operators are right-to-left associative, require a modifiable lvalue as their left operand, and return an lvalue referring to the left operand, enabling chaining. Modern C++ emphasizes move semantics and overloads for class types, allowing custom behavior for assignment. Understanding these operators is essential for efficient resource management, especially with move semantics and smart pointers, and for writing idiomatic, expressive C++ code.
